note: Upgraded from 'weak evidence' to confirmed: the primary document itself states the Council's commitment to WALGA's Declaration, resolving the previous session's access failure. Do not treat 2010 as Denmark's confirmed signing date without a dedicated council resolution record.

source: City of Joondalup Climate Change Plan 2025-2035 (PDF, directly read 2026-08-09): 'At the September 2013 City of Joondalup Council Meeting, Council endorsed the City becoming a signatory to the WALGA Climate Change Declaration.' As of April 2025 the Plan states 60 WA local governments are WALGA Declaration signatories.
note: CORRECTS the prior pass, which classified Joondalup as 'not confirmed as signatory' based on its Climate change initiatives webpage, which explicitly states the City is 'not stated as a signatory to any declaration.' The primary Climate Change Plan PDF directly contradicts that webpage. This is the clearest example in this project of why a council's own summary/landing page can be wrong about the council's own signatory status, and why coding must go to the primary planning document.

source: City of Bunbury Sustainability and Environmental Strategy 2023-2028 (PDF, directly read 2026-08-09): 'It follows the Council in 2022 signing the Western Australian Local Government Association (WALGA) Declaration on Climate Change along with adopting a Climate Change Policy, and a Council Sustainability Policy.' Restated later in the document under 'Some recent achievements': 'Climate Change Declaration: Bunbury City Council signed the Western Australian Local Government Association (WALGA) Climate Change Declaration...'
note: CORRECTS the prior pass ('not confirmed as signatory'; the council's climate-change-policy news page had returned only a JavaScript placeholder). The same document also separately names Council's support for 'WALGA's Policy Statement on Climate Change 2018' as a distinct, additional instrument, correctly distinguishing it from the Declaration — a real-world example of a council getting the P12 distinction right.
